title: Israel makes a treaty without asking God — Joshua 9
paragraphs: Israel makes a treaty without asking God — Joshua 9
They lost the moment before the battle.

In Joshua 9, Israel made peace with the Gibeonites not because God told them to — but because the deception looked believable. The bread was dry. The sandals were worn out. The story sounded right. And Scripture drops the dagger in one line: “They did not ask counsel from the LORD.” (Joshua 9:14)

Not always open rebellion.
Sometimes it’s prayerless agreement.
A decision made too fast.
A relationship welcomed too quickly.
A deal accepted because it “makes sense.”
And once Israel swore the treaty, they were bound by it.
Here’s what we miss: the enemy doesn’t always come with a sword. Sometimes he comes with a script. A reasonable voice. A tired face. A story that makes your emotions outrun your discernment.
But this text is not just about Israel’s failure. It’s about ours.

How many wounds in our lives started with this sentence:
“I thought it was okay.”
“It looked harmless.”
“I didn’t pray about it.”
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because Jesus is the better Joshua. Where we make foolish covenants, Christ keeps a perfect covenant. Where we act without asking the Father, Jesus says, “I do nothing on My own authority” (John 8:28). Our rushed decisions produce consequences. His obedience produces redemption.

So yes — Joshua 9 is a warning.
But it is also an invitation.

Slow down.
Ask God.
Test the voices.
Bring the decision into the light.
One prayer can save you from a lifetime of unnecessary entanglement.
And if you already made the wrong treaty? There is still mercy. Christ can redeem even the mess you signed with trembling hands. Repentance is not rejection. It is the road back home.

Don’t let urgency replace intimacy with God.
What looks right is not always sent by Him.
